title: Your right to a lawyer
summary: You have the right to defend yourself with a legal practitioner of your own choice, and to consult a lawyer when you are arrested.
body_plain: The Constitution guarantees that anyone facing a criminal charge may defend themselves in person or through a legal practitioner of their own choice. When you are arrested or detained, you are also entitled to remain silent until you have consulted a lawyer or any other person of your choice. If you cannot afford a lawyer, the Legal Aid Council and the Nigerian Bar Association may be able to help.
rights: You may defend yourself with a lawyer of your own choice (s.36(6)(c)).
You may stay silent until you have spoken to a lawyer (s.35(2)).
If you cannot afford one, legal aid may be available.
do_list: Ask clearly to speak to a lawyer before answering questions.
Contact Legal Aid or the NBA if you cannot afford a private lawyer.
Give your lawyer the officers' names, the station, and the time.
dont_list: Do not answer questions or sign statements while being denied a lawyer.
Do not accept that you are 'not allowed' a lawyer; it is your right.

citations.source_name: 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
